action: NSM advises assuming all secrets and named values are compromised and rotating all tokens and secrets; Microsoft advises changing potentially compromised credentials, monitoring systems they reach and reviewing logs. Check RuntimeVersion against NSM's thresholds; contact NSM on signs of compromise.
date_note: Day NSM published its notice (updated 23 November); NSM gives no earlier day for the exploitation. The Register reports Microsoft identified the issue on 18 November.
exec: NSM says organisations using Azure API Management should treat stored secrets as compromised; Microsoft says its fix does not automatically invalidate credentials used before it.
impact: NSM says it does not yet know how widely the vulnerability was exploited and has so far no evidence that deliveries at Norwegian organisations were affected.
plain: Norway's security authority says an unknown attacker went after access tokens and other secrets stored in Microsoft's Azure API Management. Microsoft says its fix does not automatically invalidate credentials used earlier.

sources.name: NSM (Norwegian National Security Authority): NSM deler tiltak mot sårbarhet i Azure API Management
Techzine Europe: Microsoft patches actively exploited vulnerability in Azure API Management

summary: Norway's NSM says an unknown actor actively went after access tokens, secrets and named values in Azure API Management, naming Equinor and Skagerak Energi among those affected. Techzine, relaying Microsoft, reports Microsoft found the flaw on 18 November and blocked the access on 19 November; the fix does not automatically invalidate credentials used earlier, and v2 tiers were not affected.
title: Norway's NSM says an unknown actor went after secrets in Azure API Management; Equinor and Skagerak Energi among affected

validation.note: NSM's own notice read (primary), with The Register (which also saw Microsoft's nonpublic advisory). Skagerak Energi's 18 November release (read, not cited) reports an attempted cyberattack but does not mention APIM; the APIM link is NSM's. No CVE was given on either page. Techzine (24 Nov) relays Microsoft's statements on dates, unaffected tiers and credentials.
